subsystems.summary: Every unit stat is a Stat(BaseValue, Type) plus a list of StatModifiers. It produces two numbers. Value (raw) = event * percentMult * (1+Σ percentAdd) * (Base+Σflat), then multiplied by Π over sources of (1+Σ preAddPostMult[source]). SpecificValue = clamp(postMult * (f_type(raw) + Σ postFlat)). f_type is a concave, piecewise power curve for MovementSpeed, Evasion, CritChance, CritDamage, GlobalAttack/Defence and BlockChance/Amount, and the identity for everything else. SuperCritDamage is a constant 2.0. Evasion, BlockChance and BlockAmount are hard-capped at 0.8. Combat reads raw Value for Health, Damage, flat/percent damage and defence, Lifesteal, AttackRange and AttackCooldown, but reads SpecificValue for probabilities and multipliers, and also for HealthRegen through a special case in UnitCore.GetStatValue. So item and crystal 'chance' bonuses that use PostFormulaFlat skip the diminishing curve, while raw-stat growth such as devour or quests goes through it. Modifiers with the same (Name, Source, ModifierType) merge into one: multiplicative types multiply, all others add, and float32 accumulation applies. Every devour reward is a single 'Devoured'/Enemy/Flat modifier per stat, so permanent growth is a plain float sum added to BaseValue before any multiplier. The aggregation core (StatBase.CalculateValue, Stat.UpdateValue/CalculateSpecificValue, AddModifier merge) has no native VA comment in this reconstruction. The ordering is corroborated by the natively annotated sibling MetaStat.CalculateValue (0x1485ef4), and the curve constants are too specific to have been invented.

subsystems.summary: Combat runs on a single hit resolver, DamageCalculator.Calculate (native VA 0x140a4cc), which has two branches. Player hits on enemies are multiplicative: (typed%Dmg x (Damage stat + item damage + typed flat + ability flat)) x (1 - ArmorConfig resist for the weapon type), then crit, super-crit, ability, event, GlobalAttack and island-medal multipliers. Enemy hits on the player go through a soft flat-defence curve, f(A, D) = A * exp(-0.75 D/A) * max(0, 1 - 0.25 D/A), so damage reaches zero once D >= 4A. In that curve D = (universal flat + matching armor items + typed flat) x typed defence% stat, which has base 1 and acts as a multiplier on flat defence, not as a percent reduction. After the curve come universal%, dodge and block rolls, rage, event, island-medal and GlobalDefence divisors. Crit, evasion, block, GlobalAttack/Defence and move speed do not use the raw stat. They use diminishing-return 'specific value' power curves; evasion and block are capped at 0.8, and super-crit damage is hard-coded to 2.0 unless post-formula modifiers apply. Pacing comes from item AttackCooldown divided by an ability attack-speed product (x2.5 vs weak or golem targets). The hit lands at an animation cast point that shifts with movement for cut and smash weapons. Enemies hit on their AttackCooldown stat inside AttackRange. The same defence curve is inverted by bisection (SolveAttackDamage) so the simulation and boss tower can calibrate enemy Damage to a target incoming DPS. Several runtime pieces are stubs: ArmorFormulas.Get, HammerRegenSystem, PlayerHitsTakenDecaySystem, CreeperExplosionSystem and UnitAutoTargetSystem.

subsystems.verdict_summary: The catalog holds up overall. I checked every expression against the code. The core resolver matches line by line: Calculate at DamageCalculator.cs:64-206 (both branches, operator order, banker's Math.Round, the event ramp, tower, rage, island and event wrappers, and Undodgeable gating). The defence curve and solver, the specific-value curves (Stat.cs:61-79), StatBase aggregation and merge, the player attack cycle and cast point, targeting, enemy regen, revive, the death checks and all four stubs also match. Line numbers are accurate except one EnemyUnit ref. Data claims I re-measured are correct: Player Config base stats, the 20 ArmorConfig assets and their resist tables, the per-asset usage counts over the 717 spawners, spawner WeaponType counts 474/147/96, spawner stats limited to types 0-5, weapon cooldowns and FlatDamage, and no prefab or scene using UnitAutoTargetSystem. Three corrections matter most. (1) SolveAttackDamage has no VA comment, so it should be reconstructed, the same as its sibling functions. (2) Lethal-ignore was misread: per-target mode does not fall back to the chance roll. (3) The claim that SimulationSystem.CalculateDefenseData matches runtime defence is false: it drops universal flat and universal armor and adds an interpolation coefficient. The island-mastery incoming half also needs to be labelled reconstructed. Smaller fixes cover the enemy attack cadence (flying enemies attack while retreating; escaping and vampire enemies never attack), the ResetCooldown and no-target cancel paths in the weapon cycle, and simulation-mode rounding and consumption. The crit-chance-buff open question is mostly answered: it flows through AbilityCritChanceBonus. Five in-scope formulas were missing: temporary modifier expiry (0x15ccda8), stun duration and its effect on enemy DPS (0x15cd31c), the 60 m far/active culling radius, the player movement displacement (0x15cbf80), and the live rescale when the player's A/B test group for the enemy HP/damage multiplier changes. I rejected nothing; every cataloged item exists in code.

subsystems.summary: Each item's stat is a two-phase piecewise-linear function of copies. Before the first evolution the item's level is its copy count: weapon damage = DamageBase[type][r] + Growth[type][r]*copies + FlatDamage, and armor = ArmorBase[r] + ArmorGrowth[r]*copies. All DamageBase arrays are 0, so a weapon's damage is just growth*copies + FlatDamage. Evolving uses up Shards[isArmor][r][L] copies and moves the item onto a hand-baked table. The stat then becomes EvolutionValue[type][r][L] + CopyValue[type][r][L]*leftoverCopies (+FlatDamage for weapons), with L capped at MaxEvolutionLevel=15. The runtime lookups are simple and reconstructed, but none of them carries a native address. The design intelligence lives in the original team's editor generators, which are all empty here. Their outputs can be reverse-fitted from the asset. The island-progress curve IslandTargetDays drives everything through a few steps. Fill rules give E_k = Start + (k-1)*Step island numbers. A native island-to-day lerp turns those into the *EvolutionTargetTimings and the interpolation TimingPoints. Evolution Values are the simulation heuristic rounded to a nice number, and CopyValue ≈ 0.5*(V[L]-V[L-1])/Shards[L]; this matches CopyValueTargetShare=0.5. Mythical rows follow V=50000*L*(L+1), copies=10L and CopyValue=5000. Balance interpolations (native) are piecewise-linear curves over that timing axis. They are summed for the additive types and multiplied for types 1 and 3. They feed simulation and boss scaling, not the item stats directly.

subsystems.verdict_summary:
I checked every cited body in Player/Inventory, Balance and the call sites, and parsed Combat Balance Config.asset and all 88 ItemConfig assets. The items catalog is substantially correct.

**Core formulas:**
- **Code:** All of these match the code exactly, including float32 evaluation order, Cut/Pierce/Smash array selection, the min(L, 15) clamp, LINQ First() lookups and the NextEvolutionLevel = Level + (Evolved ? 1 : 0) shard indexing:
  - pre-evolution weapon damage: base + growth*copies + FlatDamage
  - pre-evolution armor: base + growth*copies
  - evolved damage/armor: Value[Lc] + CopyValue[Lc]*leftover (+Flat for weapons)
  - shard cost and the evolve transition
- **Status labels:** All status labels are correct. Native comments exist only on EvolveItemCommandRunner, TryEvolve, AddItem/CreateItem/SetInitialCopies, RarityStatParam, ItemSlotKeys, HitFrameAt60Fps, BalanceInterpolation.Evaluate/ParsePoints, GetTotalCoefficient (0xf5 additive mask confirmed) and the ForecastSnapshots copy of ConvertIslandTimingToDays. The ItemModel stat math is un-annotated, so 'reconstructed' is right. Every editor generator body is empty, as claimed.

**Data claims I confirmed on the asset:**
- The base/growth arrays.
- 360/360 evolution rows over types {0,1,3,4} x rarities {0-4,6}. Magic and Divine are absent, and the Universal non-mythical rows are 1/0 placeholders.
- 90/90 shard rows with the quoted values.
- Armor rows are identical across types 0/1/3.
- Mythical rows: Value = 50000*L*(L+1), 10L copies, CopyValue 5000.
- The fill rule E_k = Start + (k-1)*Step is exact for all 10 rows.
- The island-to-day lerp reproduces every target timing (max error 1.5e-4) and the interpolation TimingPoints.
- The IslandTargetDays closed form is exact for i = 16..99.
- ReferenceShardsRequirement equals the shards table, and ReferenceStatPercent = round(100*Value/ReferenceStatValue) for all 450 rows.
- Weapon V1/pre-evolution ratio is 2.54-8.4, armor is 1.69-2.47, and the minimum armor step is 1.23.
- CopyValue is monotone in all series.
- All 19 interpolation curves.

**Corrections (minor, no rejections):**
- There are 39 *_div items, not 41.
- SimulationDpsWeaponMultiplier on armor assets is dead data.
- HitFrameAt60Fps has no consumer.
- NextLevel preview has an additional consumer and needs clamp detail.
- The pre-evolution '83000 max' is not a cap, because evolution is manual.
- The CopyValue rule is only approximate: knife and armor common deviate.
- The DropMultiplier applies only when merging into an existing item.
- The simulation DPS divides by 10 for off-type weapons.
- SimulationSystem.ConvertIslandTimingToDays is also a stub.

**Missed formulas (slot system):** weapon-type synergy counts (native), unlocked slot caps / EquippedArmors, and equip-time item StatModifier application (native, currently inert because all StatModifiers are empty).

**Out of scope but relevant to copy pacing:** Shop/ChestsModel.cs:158 gives armor chest copies = ceil(copies / ArmorCountDivider). This belongs to the shop subsystem.

subsystems.summary: Permanent growth runs through two stat containers. Player combat stats get a Flat StatModifier for each StatRewards entry when an enemy is devoured. Its value is authored Value × stat_drop[location] (MetaStat, base 1, raised by amulet-graph flats) × the zero-cooldown charge burst count × cheat × an optional ability DoubleLoot bonus × an optional VIP roll. StatBase.AddModifier merges modifiers that share (Name, Source, Type), so every devour of a class ("map.normal_mob", "map.elite", "map.tree") adds into one growing modifier. Souls (amulet currency) per devour are (max(1, 1+soul_drop_bonus) + souls_rarity_amount[soulKey]) × devour multiplier, and the Soul Pass doubles them with 25% chance. Item spawners use items_rarity_* meta stats for extra copies per kill, extra charges and a timer divisor; stat spawners subtract map_spawner_timer_reduce[location] from their cooldown. Meta stats are fed almost entirely by UpgradeModel (amulet graph and crystal upgrades). An upgrade applies f(level) as one replacing modifier, not a cumulative one, and charges PrettyRound(f_cost(level)) in a currency held by CurrencyModel. The other reward paths (granted rewards, baked GPM rewards, rewarded ads, chests) scale with the simulation's RPM per stat or with chest_level.

I checked every cited file and native annotation: MetaStat aggregation, param match, the persistence mask 0xEF0A, the calculators, the PlayerRewardSystem multipliers, the soul and item paths, UpgradeModel, PrettyRound, CurrencyModel, cashback and the rewarded-ad math all match the code, and their status labels hold. Both stubs (UpgradeMaxCapacityBonusSystem, PrepareEventRewardsCommandRunner) and the empty MetaStatsConfig.Fill are confirmed empty. Asset facts hold: 14 rewarded pools, PassDoubleSoulChance 0.25, the chest weights and the spawner counts. I reject nothing.

Corrections:
- grant_reward_stat misdescribes the bake fallback. A random or GPM reward with a SaveKey but no stored bake grants the raw Value, with no random pick and no RPM scaling.
- soul_drop_for_kill_count omits the forecast-health spawner filter, the 0.03 floor and the monotonic max.
- daily_rotation_stat does have a consumer: EventForecastService.cs:226.
- crystal_event_mob_stat_reward appends nothing when RPM ≤ 0; there is no floor of 1 in that case.
- The Health top-up condition is "not a percent type", not just "Flat".
- upgrade_total_preview filters by param only when DisplayParam is set.
- The meta stat count is 58, not 56.
- Some line references were wrong: the rewarded-ad value is at 287-297, not 309-318.

Missed formulas:
- Spawner charge top-up when capacity rises (EnemySpawner 569-585).
- Crystal chest legendary chance, 0.035 + 0.005·chest_level.
- free_chest cooldown days in ShopLotModel (native).
- Event currency and progress on devour, which bypass every multiplier.
- A second BakedStatReward writer in EventForecastService: no min-1 clamp and no command multiplier.
- Quest stat reward × stat_drop[location] (native, but tagged "candidate only").
- The per-upgrade simulation settings (SimWeight etc.), which have no consumer left in the reconstruction.

subsystems.summary: Spawners are the game's only renewable source of permanent stats, items and souls. Each of the 717 EnemySpawner configs in Main.unity sets enemy base stats (always the six stats MoveSpeed, Health, HealthRegen, Damage, AttackRange and AttackCooldown), one reward StatModifier (577 spawners; always Flat/Enemy source), and a respawn schedule. The schedule has three parts: a small cooldown between respawns, charges (each spawn uses one), and a big cooldown. In 710 spawners the big cooldown is 86400 s synced to UTC, so charges refill at UTC midnight and charges become a daily kill budget. For ordinary stat spawners (not item, VIP or event, and Cooldown>=10) the scene's Cooldown and ChargesBeforeBigRespawn are overridden at runtime by the spawner_cooldowns_v3 AB data. Non-elite: cooldown = 2(L+1) minutes capped at 30, charges = 3*Count. Elite: cooldown = 60/90/120/150 minutes for L1-4 and 180 after, charges = 2*Count. Meta upgrades cut the cooldown (map_spawner_timer_reduce, a flat subtraction), divide item-spawner cooldowns (items_rarity_timer) and add charges (items_rarity_charges). When the reduced cooldown reaches 0, one kill uses up all remaining charges and multiplies the stat and soul reward. Rewards scale as reward.Value * stat_drop[LocationNumber] * multiplier. OptimumTime, RelativeOptimumTime, AverageFightTime, Difficulty, PriorityMultiplier and HandBalance are not read by live spawning. They feed the editor balance bake (Health and Damage are solved from Difficulty and AverageFightTime) and the simulation/forecast bot. Locations are opened by gate rewards on island-boss spawners (unlockedLocation = max(unlocked, NextLocationNumber)). Island mastery gives +0.1 per medal level, up to 5, each time every eligible spawner on an island has used all its charges.

open_questions: Is the AB spawner_cooldowns_v3 default (non-elite 2(L+1) min, charges 3*Count; elite 60/90/120/150/180 min, 2*Count) what live players got, or does a remote variant override it? Scene Cooldowns are 2 minutes longer for L1-13 (min(1800, 120(L+2)) s), so it matters which one is canonical for the model.

Time unit conflict. SpawnerOptimumTimeDaysConverter (native 0x150ced0) and TimeChunkDurationMinutes use 30 playtime minutes per day. Combat Balance Config.IslandTargetDays and SimulationConfig.GetReCalcOptimumTime use 60 minutes per day (L1 30 min = 0.5, L3 240 min = 4.0). Which applies to L1-3 bakes?

One L15 spawner has Stats Health = inf in Main.unity. Check whether this is intended (an invulnerable prop) or a data error.

The EnemySpawnersDebugger 'GPM' output format is unknown (editor body missing). Check whether the serialized info list in Main.unity holds per-location gain-per-minute aggregates that could validate the yield model.

The catalog is largely accurate. I checked every formula against the code: expressions, constants, clamps and rounding in EnemySpawner (cooldown/charges/big cooldown/UTC sync/zero-cooldown collapse/item copies), the Meta calculators, the AB tables, the grant handlers, EnemyUnit, EnemyAttackSystem, EnemyRegenSystem, IslandMastery, Gates and the editor tools. No formula is rejected.

Corrections are mostly scene-fact and nuance fixes:
- 709 spawners (not 710) have BigCooldown 86400 with UTC sync; the creeper uses a rolling 24 h.
- Elite scene cooldowns are min(180, 30(L+2)) min, not 'mostly 10800'.
- 569 spawners are AB-eligible.
- 22 one-shot spawners get AB charges 3.
- The Health=Infinity spawner is a BossTower item spawner.
- All 10 VIP spawners have RequiredVipLevel 3, so a VIP-level check is likely missing.
- GateLocationTrigger uses a serialized locationNumber at runtime; the NextLocationNumber-isExit relation is editor-only.

- The difficulty_semantics bake expression lacked crit, ability coefficients, the resist clamp and the round-to-10 damage. That bake is native (0x13db16c) and belongs as recovered_native under simulation.
- '../' code_ref prefixes should be dropped.

- geode timer reduction per kill (KillCount = extra charges + multiplier)
- far-distance culling that disables enemy regen and AI (60/30 units)
- an IsDummy contradiction that stops the dummy spawner from ever spawning

subsystems.summary: The simulation subsystem is the original team's offline balancing pipeline. A bot (SimulationSystem) plays the map greedily with a time model of 10 minutes of play followed by 230 minutes AFK, then one chunk per day from day 4. It writes the simulated player's power (stats, DPS per weapon type, defense per damage type, items, and RPM, the rewards per minute for each stat) to Simulation Data as 63 snapshots indexed by play minutes and 46 snapshots indexed by day. Those snapshots were trimmed to roughly 10% geometric spacing. Every spawner's Health and Damage is then baked from the snapshot at its OptimumTime. OptimumTime is set as island start day + RelativeOptimumTime × island duration. Health is chosen so the player's crit- and ability-scaled DPS against the enemy's weakest armor kills the group in AverageFightTime. Damage is chosen so the group takes Difficulty × player HP (plus battle regen) over AverageFightTime, after inverting the exp/linear defense curve, with evasion, block and the ability EHP curve applied. The BalanceInterpolation curves are configured by island and converted to days. They scale everything as time-dependent multipliers: type 2 is an additive flat bonus (+3.0 by day 405), type 3 is a multiplicative bonus (×4.9 by day 405), and types 4/5 are the ability DPS/EHP multipliers. At runtime the same machinery computes RPM, which scales stat, shop and event rewards. The Forecast module re-uses the baked snapshots to auto-balance crystal-event golems and bosses. I re-ran the recovered bake formula against the shipped Simulation Data and it reproduces the shipped scene spawner HP within 5% for 552 of 706 spawners. 79 match exactly, 79 of the 102 minute-mode spawners. The SpawnerBakeInfos log in Simulation Config is an older, stale bake.

open_questions: Recomputing the recovered bake on the shipped Simulation Data matches scene Health exactly for 79 of 706 spawners, within 5% for 552, and damage within 5% for 504. Only 9 of 53 day-mode spawners that sit exactly on a stored chunk index match exactly. So the scene may have been baked from untrimmed Simulation Config.TimeChunkSnapshots (now empty) or from a slightly different sim run, or hand-tweaked afterwards. Which source is authoritative for the model?

SpawnerBakeInfos in Simulation Config is clearly stale: only 5 rows equal the scene and late-game values are up to 30× lower. Should it be ignored entirely, or kept as history of an earlier balance pass?

TimeChunkDurationMinutes=30 is used to convert minute-based optimum times (SimulationSystem.cs:537, BossSpawnService.cs:449) into chunk indices, but stored TimeChunkIndex values count days (1440 min = SpawnerChargesChunkMinutes). Is this a legacy unit bug, or did tower floors intentionally use 30-minute units?

For minute-mode (IsDays=0) bakes, the timing passed to the ability curves is minutes/60, which is hours, not days. This is harmless only because the type 4/5 curves are 0 before day 20. Is that intended?

In the game outside simulation, GetBalanceTimingMinutes reads Simulation Config.CurrentTotalPlaytime/CurrentPlaytime, which are 0. Runtime RPM, DpsData and the ability multipliers are therefore evaluated at day 0, not the player's real day. Did the original runtime set these fields from the real playtime somewhere?

The bot loop (Tick/FastTick/FindBestSpawner/ProcessInventory/priority) is entirely missing, so Simulation Data cannot be regenerated after economy changes. A replacement progression model must be re-implemented, using the recovered fight model, RPM and bake as building blocks.

The forecast damage target uses ×(1−dodge) with no attack cooldown or attacker count. The spawner bake uses cooldown/(1−evasion) and divides by attackers. Is the difference intentional for event bosses?

The bake picks player defense by the location's PreferredWeaponType, but BossTower.BakeStatsForFloor uses the spawner's WeaponType and the lowest-resist armor rather than the best player score. Which convention should the model treat as canonical?

RPM divides daily obtainable reward (reward × charges) by 60. That fits the 60 active minutes/day lifecycle in the early days, but fast-tick days average about 46 active minutes. Was 60 a deliberate design constant?
HandBalance=1 on two spawners (Spawner_1_8dc2006722e6c994593946eef6f4f007, second_biome_door). Was this the rebake opt-out flag? The rebake code is missing.

ForecastHelper.SetEventSettings and the EventBossCount/EventBossGamma/EventLastBossMinute inputs are unused in the recovered code. The original probably generated EventBossMinutes from a gamma curve, but the exact formula is unknown.

Amulet simulation (AmuletSimulationMultipliers, AmuletLevelBalance, AmuletConfig.BakeAmuletAutoBalance) left no data in Simulation Config. Any baked amulet economy must be recovered from Amulet Config directly.
subsystems.verdict_summary:
The catalog is accurate overall. I checked every expression against the code: Evaluate/GetTotalCoefficient, the fight model, the old and new RPM, soul RPM, DpsData/DefenseData, fast and slow spawner DPS, BuildSpawnerBakeReport (HP and damage), GetReCalcOptimumTime, snapshot interpolation and nearest lookup, and the forecast BuildCore/BuildAutoBalancedEnemies/ramp/reward/crystal mapping. Constants, clamps, rounding and status labels are correct. The native VA comments are present wherever the catalog says recovered_native, and the stub and editor_only bodies really are empty. Code_ref line numbers are correct, except DamageCalculator 77-78, which should be 78-79.

Data claims also check out: 46 trimmed chunk indices that fit 10% geometric spacing, TimeChunkIndex = floor(Total/1440), K2 = 3.0 and K3 = 4.9075 at day 405, K2 = 0.20397 at day 3, the island→timing conversion of the curves, 604/609 RelativeOptimumTime fits, 5/712 stale SpawnerBakeInfos rows, and HandBalance on 2 spawners. My independent re-bake gives HP exact 79 (all minute-mode), within 1% 246, within 5% 555 of 716; damage exact 124 and within 5% 511. That matches the reported 79/246/552/118/504.

Corrections:
- The attacker factor min(4,(Count+1)/2) uses float division, so Count=2 gives 1.5.
- The bot's cooldown filter applies only while IsRunning, and runtime always uses GPM-bot mode.
- The ChargesTotal derivation was incomplete: it is AB charges×Count, or ChargesBeforeBigRespawn plus the meta items_rarity_charges bonus; DisableAfterFirstClear spawners are never used at runtime.
- Snapshot feature fields are K2/K3 only for MainInterpolationStats.
- Minute snapshots are about 1.1 min apart in the first cycle, not 5 min.
- The open-question claim that 9 of 53 on-chunk day-mode spawners match is wrong. 0 of 54 match HP and 0 of 608 day-mode spawners match exactly. Trimming therefore cannot explain the drift; the day-mode scene values come from a different simulation run.
- The gamma-curve guess for EventBossMinutes contradicts the shipped data.
- The slow spawner-DPS path uses the spawner's own WeaponType.

I added two missed entries: the spawner charges limit (a recovered_native RPM multiplier) and the local forecast fallback snapshot. No formulas rejected.

subsystems.summary: Powerups add combat power through three systems: the Amulet upgrade graph, Rage, and item Abilities. Rewarded-ad stat grants are covered too. The Amulet is a permanent skill tree of 298 nodes, defined in code by AmuletUpgradeDefsBuilder with native per-level lambdas. Each level of a node sets an absolute value, not a sum of earlier levels: value(L) = f(L) * StatModifierMultipliers[key]. The cost to reach level L is PrettyRound(c(L) * UpgradeCostMultipliers[key]), paid in souls. Both multiplier dictionaries in Amulet Config.asset are the baked output of an editor auto-balance tool that was not in the APK. Paid soul costs become amulet XP (BaseExperience[soul] * souls). That XP sets amulet level 1-7 through cumulative thresholds, and the level gates which nodes can be bought. At full tree the amulet gives about +13.59M flat Health, +0.6-0.8 PreAdditivePostMultiplicative % per damage/defence type, and post-formula flat +6% crit/evasion/block. It also provides keystone meta stats that feed Rage (extra health, damage reduction, extra hits), marks, lightning and the economy proc chance. Rage is a 0-3 level (4 in the Berserker boss fight) per-fight buff. It fills from AddRageEffect procs on hit against fixed thresholds [30,100,270,270], decays after 10 s without gain, and is unlocked by GrantRageAccessEffect on items. Its strength comes entirely from amulet meta stats and crystal legendaries. Abilities are data-driven (AbilityDef in item assets): value/chance/stacks are tier overrides chosen by item stars plus per-frame boosts, multiplied by a ValueScaler. Each frame they rebuild multiplicative per-weapon and per-player damage, attack-speed, crit and regen factors. They also add one-shot next-hit/empower bonuses, lightning, marks, shock, thorns and heals, and can grant permanent stats as rewards. Rewarded ads grant a permanent flat stat equal to round(2x? * 0.5 * RPM[stat] * 6 * locMult).

open_questions: DoubleLootEffect sets AbilityState.DoubleLoot=true (3 data instances), but nothing in the reconstruction reads it; the comment says PlayerRewardSystem consumes it. Is the doubling of stat rewards missing from PlayerRewardSystem?

PlayerModel.AbilityHealthRegenMultiplier (HealthRegenForMissingHealthEffect) is only read by UI/Inventory/InventoryStatView.cs:64. The runtime player regen tick that should multiply by it is not found.
HammerRegenSystem is a full stub (hammer_regen meta = 0.001L from graph_hammer_regen_3_3). What are the original formula and its weapon condition?
ScaledMultiplierEffect, GrantStatOnHitEffect and TreatAsAllSlotsEmptyEffect are stubs. No current asset uses them, but the original bodies are unknown.

AmuletConfig.BakeAmuletAutoBalance and the static AutoBalanceStatTypes set are missing. The algorithm that maps LevelTargetDays, AutoBalance* and per-node SimulationSettings to UpgradeCostMultipliers/StatModifierMultipliers needs reconstructing before amulet numbers can be re-tuned consistently.

RageModel (thresholds 30/100/270/270, 10 s decay, TryAddRage), RageExtraHealthSystem, RageExtraHitSystem and AddRageEffect have no native-address annotations and should be verified against the binary.
RequiredExperiencePerLevel has 7 entries but only 6 are reachable at MaxLevel=7. Was a level 8 planned, or is the index offset (level-2) intentional?
AmuletModel.TryFillWithSoul checks for 1 huge soul but does not spend it. The comment says this is native behavior; confirm it is intended design.
RageExtraHitSystem picks the weapon by item.Damage, while ResetCooldown and TriggerHighestDamageWeapon pick by DPS. Confirm this difference against native code.
subsystems.verdict_summary:
The catalog is largely accurate. I checked all 36 formulas against the code and found no rejections. I re-derived the amulet numbers with a script that parses all 298 AmuletUpgradeDefsBuilder defs and the baked multipliers in Amulet Config.asset. Stat totals, meta lambda values, XP thresholds, and the native/stub status labels all hold up.

Corrections:
- **Amulet cost (main defect):** cost is PrettyRound(PrettyRound(c(L)) * CM), not single-rounded. UpgradeCostDef.Evaluate already rounds before UpgradeDef.EvaluateCosts multiplies. This changes non-integer shapes such as L^1.5 and L^1.2. Corrected totals: elite 84,435 (not ~84.6k), common 12,143,385, XP 41.59M.
- **Two open questions are wrong:** the AbilityHealthRegenMultiplier consumer exists (PlayerRegenSystem.cs:36), and DoubleLoot is consumed in PlayerRewardSystem.cs:55-63.
- **Callers that do not exist:** no code calls AddSouls(isSimulation=true) or AmuletModel.AddLevels. Their used_by claims are unsupported.
- **AddStatEffect:** the daily-proc check comes before the temporary branch too.
- **Ability conditions:** CombatCondition has a Mode inversion and StacksCondition has a NotReachedMax mode; both were missing. The cooldown tick lives in ResetPerFrameState.
- **Lightning:** its base damage is the already-mitigated hit damage.
- **Line numbers:** many code_refs are off (AbilityState, AbilityExecuteEventSystem, AddRageEffect, AbilityContext, builder lambdas at 1958-3214).

Missed formulas added:
- the DoubleLoot multiplier;
- the trigger-routing mask, which makes OnHit/OnCrit procs fire only from the owning weapon while OnPostHit is broadcast;
- TriggerAbilityEffect chaining;
- the item ability unlock gate (Evolved and UnlockLevel).

critic_summary:
The catalog covers the core combat and growth loop well. The main gaps are cross-couplings and simulation and editor stubs, not missing combat math.

**Key missed couplings**
1. Item-spawner copies overwrite the per-kill multiplier. Item drop amount therefore also scales devour stat and soul income (EnemySpawner.cs:1215, GrantSpawnerStatRewardCommandHandler.cs:29, GrantSpawnerSoulRewardCommandHandler.cs:33). The simulated RPM does not model this.
2. Weapon cadence modifiers sit outside the attack-cycle entries: the 1 s equip warm-up, the weapon_1 base-range gate, and the ability cooldown reset (cooldown = castPoint*cd + 0.15).
3. Meta mark synergies (evasion_mark, mark_lifesteal, the hard-coded 10% piercing mark chance) and state-dependent effects (missing-health, empty-slot and stat-proportional damage, temporary buffs) cannot be represented in the expected-value simulation or bake. They enter the design only through the PlayerAbilityDPSMult and EHPMult interpolation curves.

**Status audit (correct labels before export)**
These files carry no native VA comments, so their formulas should be `reconstructed`, not `recovered_native`, unless other evidence exists:

formulas.name: Raw stat value aggregation (StatBase.CalculateValue)
formulas.expression: Value = E * M * A * (Base + F) * PROD_s (1 + P_s); where F = SUM v[Flat], A = 1 + SUM v[PercentAdditive], M = PROD v[PercentMultiplicative] (raw factors, NOT 1+v), E = PROD (1 + eventBonus%(v[EventPercent])/100), P_s = SUM v[PreAdditivePostMultiplicative] grouped by ModifierSource s. PostFormula* types are ignored here. No rounding, no caps.

formulas.name: Flat defence mitigation curve (ApplyDamageDefense)
formulas.expression: r = D / A ; incoming(A, D) = A * exp(-0.75 * r) * max(0, 1 - 0.25 * r)   (returns 0 if A <= 0). Damage is 0 when D >= 4A; at D = A it is 0.354 A; at D = 0.5A it is 0.601 A

variables.meaning: attacker raw attack damage (after event ramp / tower reduction)

formulas.status_evidence: No VA comment on the method. Its operand order (ratio*-0.75, ratio*-0.25+1.0) looks like decompiler FMA output. Native-annotated callers (SimulationSystem.GetSpawnerDps, VA 0x13ef8d4) use the same function, and SimulationSystem.CalculateDefenseData builds D the same way.
formulas.notes: Constants 0.75 and 0.25 are the main defence tuning levers and have no config source. f is monotonic in A, which is what makes the bisection inverse well defined.

formulas.name: Inverse defence: attack needed for target incoming damage
formulas.expression: find minimal A (absolute tolerance 1.0) s.t. forward(A) >= T; forward(A) = incoming(A, D) * p. Algorithm: upper = 1; while forward(upper) < T: upper *= 2; then bisect [0, upper] until upper - lower <= 1; return upper

variables.meaning: percent multiplier applied after the curve

formulas.output: enemy attack Damage stat value that yields T after defence
formulas.status_evidence: No VA comment, but the body contains decompiler artifacts: an int.MaxValue loop counter and Debug.LogError(upper) on exhaustion. It is clearly a port of native control flow.
formulas.notes: This formula ties authored enemy Damage values to the designer's intended incoming DPS. If combat.flat_defense_curve changes, every baked enemy Damage becomes stale.

formulas.name: BalanceInterpolation piecewise-linear curve
formulas.expression: T = parse(TimingPoints), C = parse(CoefPoints) (split ';', invariant float). If |T|<2 or |C|<2 or |T|!=|C| -> 0 (error). If x <= T0 -> C0. Else for the first segment i with T[i+1] >= x: p = clamp01((x - T[i])/(T[i+1]-T[i])) (p=0 if T[i]==T[i+1]); value = C[i] + p*(C[i+1]-C[i]). If x > T_last -> C_last (flat extrapolation both ends).

formulas.name: Stat reward-per-minute (RPM/GPM), current algorithm
formulas.expression: (F, L) = FastRPMParams(fightTimeSeconds, maxHealthLossMultiplier) = (10, 1) variant A / (15, 5) variant B. For spawners s with a StatReward of type k, skipping those with loss_s = -healthDelta_s > L*HPmax: c_s = F/(F + fightTime_s) * reward_s(k) * charges_s * locMult_s * hpMult_s, where charges_s = DisableAfterFirstClear ? Count : ChargesTotal; locMult = 2 for non-elite spawners on locations 1-2, else 1; hpMult = sqrt(HPmax/loss_s) if loss_s > HPmax else 1. RPM_k = SUM c_s / 60; if RPM_k > 0 then RPM_k = max(0.5, RPM_k); RPM_k *= AB RpmStatValueMultiplier(k) (attack {6,8,12}, armor {14,16,20}, sustain {1,2,22}); RPM_k = max(RPM_k, previous RPM_k) (monotonic).

formulas.name: Stat RPM, old greedy-1000s algorithm
formulas.expression: Candidates with reward k and playerRPS>0, sorted by playerRPS desc; budget 1000 s: for j-th candidate: time = farmedTime + 2*j / S(MovementSpeed); fights = min(1000/(BaseCooldown*Count), (1000 - T)/time); T += time*fights; R += fights*reward(k)*Count; stop when T >= 999.9. RPM_k = min(1, 1000/T) * R / max(1000, T) * 60; if >0 then max(0.5, .); monotonic max with previous.

(2) Evasion mark: on a dodge, if any Stabbing weapon is equipped, apply floor(evasion_mark) marks to the attacker. (3) Mark lifesteal: on a player hit against a target with s > 0 mark stacks, lsFlat *= 1 + mark_lifesteal * s and lsPct *= 1 + mark_lifesteal * s. (Hydra target: an extra lsFlat *= 1 + 0.1 * s, BossTower, out of scope.) Then heal = lsFlat * (1 + NextHitLifestealFlatBonus) + lsPct * HPmax, capped at HPmax.
formulas.output: Mark application rate and lifesteal multiplier
formulas.status_evidence: All three sites carry 'Native' ELF VA comments.
formulas.notes: The 10% base piercing mark chance is hard-coded. If stats.lifesteal_player / combat.player_lifesteal_on_hit omit the mark_lifesteal multiplier, those entries are incomplete. Note that the general ApplyLifesteal (enemy on player) does not cap health, while the player path caps at HPmax.

formulas.name: Damage and regen scaling with missing health
formulas.expression: missingPct = (1 - HP / specific(Health)) * 100. DamageForMissingHealthEffect: for each equipped weapon (optionally only WeaponType X), AbilityDamageMultiplier *= 1 + missingPct * v. HealthRegenForMissingHealthEffect: AbilityHealthRegenMultiplier *= 1 + missingPct * v. Neither has a clamp. Player regen per second = HealthRegen * AbilityHealthRegenMultiplier.
formulas.output: Per-frame weapon damage and regen multipliers
formulas.status_evidence: Annotated 'Native 0x15ef3cc' / 'Native 0x15f0ae4'.
formulas.notes: Merge into powerups.weapon_damage_multipliers / heal_effects if they already enumerate these effects. The expected-value models (simulation, bake) cannot represent HP-state-dependent multipliers, which is a structural gap in the model.

formulas.name: Empty-slot and stat-proportional damage / attack-speed effects
formulas.expression: E = |{slots: unlocked and not equipped}|. DamageForEmptySlots: ownerItem.AbilityDamageMultiplier *= 1 + v * E. AttackSpeedForEmptySlots: ownerItem.AbilityAttackSpeedMultiplier *= 1 + v * E. ValueScaler 'empty slots' source: E, or the total slot count if TreatAsAllSlotsEmpty. DamageForStat: b = v * specific(SourceStat). If AffectSpecificSlot: the item in SlotKey gets AbilityDamageFlat += b (ModifierType Flat) or AbilityDamageMultiplier *= 1 + b. Otherwise the player gets AbilityDamageFlat += b or AbilityDamageMultiplier *= 1 + b.
formulas.output: Per-frame weapon damage / attack-speed multipliers and flat ability damage
formulas.status_evidence: Annotated with native/original ELF VAs.
formulas.notes: This creates a design coupling: unlocking a slot raises E (more damage) until an item is equipped there. Merge into the aggregate powerups.* entries if they already include it.

formulas.name: Temporary weapon buff (timed damage / attack-speed / crit)
formulas.expression: On trigger: bonus_T = ValueScaler(ValueScaling), with MovementSpeed as the default scaling stat, and timer_T = Duration (default 7 s). The new bonus replaces the old one; it does not stack. Each frame, for every T with timer_T > 0: timer_T -= dt. When it expires, bonus_T = 0. Otherwise: Damage gives owner.AbilityDamageMultiplier *= 1 + bonus. AttackSpeed gives owner.AbilityAttackSpeedMultiplier *= 1 + bonus. CritDamage gives owner.AbilityCritMultiplier *= 1 + bonus. CritChance gives owner.AbilityCritChanceBonus += bonus.
formulas.status_evidence: Original ELF VA annotations on Execute/UpdatePassive/ctor.
config_params: AbilityDef TemporaryWeaponBuffEffect (3 uses): BuffType, Duration, ValueScaling
formulas.notes: Uptime = min(1, Duration * procRate). Steady-state models must convert proc rate into uptime. Merge if already inside the aggregate ids.

formulas.name: Starting weapon and auto-equip policy
formulas.expression: On first unit init with no items: grant and equip PlayerConfig.StartingWeapon. AddItem(item): if an item with the same Config.Key exists, existing.Copies += DropMultiplier * item.Copies and nothing is equipped. Otherwise the item is appended and EquipItem picks the first slot with !IsEquipped && IsUnlocked && SlotType == item.SlotType. A new item is equipped only if a free unlocked slot exists. It never replaces an equipped item. Equip triggers WearingTime = 0, adds Config.StatModifiers and recalculates rage access.
formulas.output: Which items contribute to live DPS/armor
formulas.status_evidence: Methods annotated with native ELF VAs.
formulas.notes: The live game depends on player loadout choices. The simulation (CalculateDpsData) instead picks the top UnlockedWeaponSlots weapons by (type match, DPS) and divides off-type DPS by 10. The model should treat the loadout as optimal per the simulation rule, not this auto-equip rule.

formulas.name: Devour animation delay before rewards
formulas.expression: t_reward = floatingTime + catchingTime when the animation completes, or at most floatingTime + catchingTime + 0.5 s (FinishTimeout). The prefab values are floatingTime = 0.4 and catchingTime = 0.4, so t_reward is about 0.8 s, max 1.3 s. Stat, soul and currency rewards are granted in HandleDevour, not at death.
formulas.output: Latency between kill and stat or soul grant
formulas.status_evidence: PlayerDevour update loop annotated 'Native ELF VA 0x1443484'.
formulas.notes: This is small, but it is per-kill overhead that the simulation folds into its constant RPM tuple (70, 50, 2, 2). It matters for fast-kill spawners (fight time of 1-2 s).

formulas.name: Simulated rewarded-ad income in the bot
formulas.expression: Intended: every AdsIntervalMinutes of simulated playtime, grant a stat reward worth AdsRewardMultiplierInMinutes * RPM(stat). Body missing. With the shipped config AdsRewardMultiplierInMinutes = 0 and AdsIntervalMinutes = 6, the baked Simulation Data contains no ad income.
formulas.output: Extra stat income in the simulated progression
formulas.status_evidence: ProcessSimulateAds() has an empty body. No other reference to AdsRewardMultiplierInMinutes or AdsIntervalMinutes exists.
formulas.notes: Live rewarded ads (meta.rewarded_ad_stat_value = RPM*6*...) are therefore not reflected in the baked balance target. Real players who watch ads are ahead of the curve.

formulas.name: Bot stat / item benefit weights
formulas.expression: statsBenefit[s] is initialized to 1 for every StatType, and itemBenefit[item] is the item value. Both are meant to be updated by CalculateStatBenefit and ModifyFromItem (marginal power gain per unit of stat or item), whose bodies are missing. Consumer: rewardValue(spawner) = Count * (Σ_r statsBenefit[r.StatType] * r.Value), or for item spawners Count * (value + itemBenefit[item]) with a fallback of 10000 if the item is not owned. currentBoss gets 1e6.
formulas.output: Spawner reward value used for bot target choice
formulas.status_evidence: CalculateStatBenefit() is empty and ModifyFromItem returns default. The consumer CalculateSpawnerRewardValue is native-annotated.
formulas.notes: Without the weights, a rerun bot values all stats equally (1.0), so the farm path and therefore the baked growth curve cannot be regenerated faithfully. Treat Simulation Data snapshots as ground truth.

formulas.name: Simulated item copy emission and fractional rolls
formulas.expression: Intended: copies per simulated clear = RollFractionalCount(baseCount * GetItemEmissionCoefficient(timing, item) * (IsPreferredItemEmissionType(item) ? k : 1)), with chained-item base counts from GetChainedItemBaseCount(baseItemsCount, value). RollFractionalCount(x) is presumably floor(x) + Bernoulli(frac(x)). All bodies return 0 or false.
formulas.output: Simulated item copies, which drive simulated evolution timing
formulas.status_evidence: All five methods return default constants.
config_params: Combat Balance Config.Interpolations (item emission types if present)
formulas.notes: This is the missing link between spawner item drops and the EvolutionShardsRequirements and EvolutionTargetTimings tables. Those tables are output-only data (editor_only_missing generators).

formulas.name: Bot fight resolution, regen and death handling
formulas.expression: Intended per bot step: choose best = FindBestSpawner() by priority; resolve fights via SimulateFightWithSpawner / SimulateFightWithSpawnerFast(fights): time += farmedTime * fights, HP += healthDelta * fights, then ApplyRegen(seconds): HP = min(HPmax, HP + regen * seconds). ProcessDeath on HP <= 0. Efficiency helpers GetFightEfficiency, GetTotalDPS, GetTotalArmor, CalculateFarmPotencial(spawner, path, damage) and CalcDifficultSpawner(spawner, secondsRegen). All bodies are missing.
formulas.output: Simulated time and HP evolution, which produce Simulation Data snapshots
formulas.status_evidence: Empty or default-return bodies. Only GetRegen/GetBattleRegen/CalculateSpawnerData around them are native.
formulas.notes: Merge into simulation.player_progression_tick if that entry already enumerates these stubs. TimeStep (300), SimulationSpeed, UseFastTick and FastTickStartChunkOffset have no live consumer.

formulas.name: Simulated spawner charge budget per day chunk
formulas.expression: chunk = floor(CurrentTotalPlaytime / SpawnerChargesChunkMinutes) with SpawnerChargesChunkMinutes = 1440. In charges mode, a spawner is eligible while used[s] < limit(s), where limit = Count if DisableAfterFirstClear, else ChargesTotal. Intended reset: on chunk rollover, used[s] = 0 (UpdateSpawnerChargesChunk, ResetCooldowns), with each clear consuming GetSpawnerChargesPerClear(s) charges. The reset and per-clear bodies are missing.

variables.meaning: charge reset period in simulated minutes

formulas.output: Which spawners the bot may farm in the current simulated day
formulas.status_evidence: UpdateSpawnerChargesChunk and ResetCooldowns are empty, and GetSpawnerChargesPerClear returns 0. The limit and timing functions are native.
formulas.notes: This complements the already-missed simulation.spawner_charges_limit. Note the unit mismatch: optimum 'days' are 30-minute time chunks (TimeChunkDurationMinutes = 30, ConvertOptimumToDays = minutes/30), while charges reset every 1440 simulated minutes.

formulas.name: AB stat-class RPM multiplier and fast-RPM parameters
formulas.expression: rpm(stat) *= m(stat), where m = sustainMult for {Health, HealthRegen, LifestealFlat}, attackMult for {StabDamageFlat, CutDamageFlat, BuckshotDamageFlat}, armorMult for {StabDefenceFlat, CutDefenceFlat, BuckshotDefenceFlat}, and 1 otherwise. The fast RPM parameters (fightTimeSeconds T and maxHealthLossMultiplier L) enter the time-chunk RPM as contribution = T / (T + fightTime) * value * charges * locMult * hpMult, where a spawner is skipped if loss > L * HP. The location multiplier locMult is 2 for islands 1-2 (non-elite) and 1 otherwise.

variables.source: ABTest Data Config.asset CommonRewardMultipliers (all 1 in default variant)
ABTest Data Config.asset FastRPMParams (10 / 1 default; variant 15 / 5)

formulas.output: Stat RPM/GPM used by all RPM-valued rewards
formulas.status_evidence: ABTestService has no native annotation. The SimulationSystem consumers are native-annotated.
formulas.notes: The extractor must export ABTest Data Config.asset (all variants and per-location overrides). Scene and config values alone do not determine live RPM, enemy HP/damage, spawner cooldowns or charges.

formulas.name: GrantStatOnHit / TreatAsAllSlotsEmpty / ScaledMultiplier effect stubs
formulas.expression: GrantStatOnHitEffect.Execute: intended to add a StatModifier(StatType, ModifierType, Source, value) on hit; body empty. TreatAsAllSlotsEmptyEffect.Execute: intended to set PlayerModel.TreatAsAllSlotsEmpty = true; body empty. The flag is reset every frame in AbilityExecuteEventSystem and read in ValueScaler (empty-slot count = all slots).
formulas.status_evidence: Empty Execute/UpdatePassive bodies.
formulas.notes: An asset scan (grep 'class: <Type>' over *.asset) finds 0 uses of GrantStatOnHitEffect, TreatAsAllSlotsEmptyEffect, ScaledMultiplierEffect and EmptySlotsCondition, so these stubs have zero impact on current numbers. Track them only as a risk for future content.

formulas.name: WeaponAttackTiming helper (windup/travel/hit ratios)
formulas.expression: Constants: windup = travel = return = 1/3, hitElapsedRatio = 2/3, hitCooldownRatio = 0.3333333. All Get*Duration and GetHitCooldownThreshold(attackCooldown, animationDurationCap, ...) methods return 0. The intended form is presumably hitElapsed = min(attackCooldown, cap) * normalized(windup + travel * progress).
formulas.status_evidence: Every method returns 0f, and grep finds no callers of WeaponAttackTiming.*.
formulas.notes: The live hit threshold is the native PlayerAttackSystem.GetHitCooldownThreshold = castPoint * AttackCooldown (0x1440f74), so this stub does not change gameplay numbers. It is listed so nobody wires it in by mistake.

formulas.name: Shield armor values synced to a leader item (editor)
formulas.expression: Editor rule, body absent. When SyncShieldValuesByLeader is true, the shield EvolutionArmorValues / ArmorBase rows are presumably copied or scaled from a 'leader' armor row (helmet or same rarity) during auto-balance, giving armor(shield, r, e) = armor(leader, r, e).
formulas.status_evidence: The field has no consumer anywhere in CodeBase.
formulas.notes: Also note that GetArmorBase and GetArmorGrowthPerLevel ignore damageType (they index by rarity only), so pre-evolution helmets and shields of equal rarity have identical armor.

formulas.name: Evolution auto-balance guard multipliers (unconsumed levers)
formulas.expression: Presumed generator constraints: copyValue_e >= MinCopyValueGrowthMultiplier * copyValue_{e-1}; copyValue share of the evolution step = CopyValueTargetShare; value_e >= MinEvolutionValueFromShardsMultiplier * (value gained from shards before evolution); armorValue_e >= MinArmorEvolutionValueFromPreviousEvolutionMultiplier * armorValue_{e-1}.

variables.meaning: min growth of copy value between evolutions
target share of copies in evolution value

formulas.status_evidence: The four fields have no consumer, and ApplyEvolutionAutoBalance / FillRemainingEvolutionValues / SetEvolutionValue are empty.
formulas.notes: If balance.evolution_value_autobalance already lists these four config_params, fold this entry into it. They can be validated empirically against the exported EvolutionCombatValue rows (ratio checks).

formulas.name: Amulet level target days and auto-balance multipliers (unconsumed)
formulas.expression: Bake target: amulet level L should be reached at day LevelTargetDays[L-1] = [20, 26, 34, 56, 90, 130, 180]. The feature is available from FeatureUnlockDay = 16. RequiredExperiencePerLevel and the graph cost multipliers are solved so that the cumulative simulated soul XP at LevelTargetDays matches, scaled by AutoBalanceCostMultiplier (1.25) and AutoBalanceExperienceMultipliers[L] (0.8, ...).
formulas.status_evidence: FeatureUnlockDay, LevelTargetDays, AutoBalanceCostMultiplier and AutoBalanceExperienceMultipliers have no consumers, and BakeAmuletAutoBalance is empty.
formulas.notes: The runtime unlock gate is UnlockLocationNumber (8), not FeatureUnlockDay. Merge into powerups.amulet_autobalance_bake if it already cites these fields.

formulas.name: Numeric config fields with no consumer
formulas.expression: No formula reads these fields. EnemySpawnerConfig.WanderRadius, EnemySpawnerConfig.WanderDwellTime, EnemySpawnerConfig.NonSelectable, ItemConfig.Number (UI only), SimulationConfig.MaxSimultaneousAttackers (const 4; code uses a literal min((Count+1)/2, 4)), SimulationConfig.SnapshotInterval, SimulationConfig.TimeStep, SimulationConfig.SimulationSpeed, SimulationConfig.UseFastTick and SimulationConfig.FastTickStartChunkOffset (bot stubs), and LocationConfig.PreferredArmorType (outside Quests/Events/UI).
